title: WPCRL/193/2019 of ADIL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
MCRC No. 2274 of 2023
In
WPCRL No. 193 of 2019
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Ms. Mamta Rani, Advocate, holding
brief of Mr. Avidit Noliyal, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. V.S. Rawat, Brief Holder for the
State.
Ms. Divya Jain, Advocate for the
applicant in recall application.
Instant petition was decided on
21.07.2020 on the basis of statement given
by learned counsel for the parties that the
matter has been amicably settled. Based
on it, FIR No. 194 of 2018, Police Station
Cantt. District Dehradun has been
quashed.
Now a recall application has been
filed alongwith the delay condonation
application. According to the recall
application, the charge sheet has already
been filed in the matter. Therefore, the writ
petition had rendered infructuous on
21.07.2020. According to the recall
application, the order dated 21.07.2020
passed in the instant matter erroneously
records the consent of the learned counsel
for the respondent no.3 that he matter has
been compromised.
It is the case of the review applicant
that he came to know about the order
dated 21.07.2020 only when he applied for
a certified copy of the order because he had
not received summon in the matter from
the court concerned.
Heard.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
would submit that she had never
consented for compromise and it has been
erroneously recorded in the impugned
order that learned counsel for the

respondent no.3 did not contravene the
factum of compromise between the parties.
On 21.07.2020, the Court passed the
following order:-
Ms. Prabha Naithani, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. P.S. Bohara, A.G.A. along with Mr.
Siddhartha Bisht, Mrs. Shivangi Gangwar and
Mrs. Preeta Bhatt, Brief Holders for the State.
Ms. Divya Jain, Advocate for respondent
no.3. By means of present writ petition,
petitioner has sought a writ of certiorari for
quashing of FIR dated 23.12.2018 registered
as case crime no.194 of 2018 at P.S. Cantt,
District Dehradun, under sections 420, 467,
468, 471 IPC.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that the matter has been amicably
settled between the parties. Learned counsel
for respondent no.3 does not contradict the
said fact and states that in view of
compromise between the parties, respondent
no.3 does not want to pursue the present
criminal proceedings against the petitioner.
As per the statement made by learned
counsel for the respective parties, both the
parties have entered into a compromise. In
such circumstances, ordinarily it is
appropriate to quash the FIR. Even otherwise,
I have gone through the papers brought on
record and on a bare perusal of the FIR, it
transpires that no case is made out against
the petitioner under the aforesaid section.
In view of the above, writ petition is
allowed. Impugned FIR dated 23.12.2018
registered as case crime no.194 of 2018 at
P.S. Cantt, District Dehradun, under sections
420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, is hereby quashed.
No order as to costs.
Recall of the above order was sought
on the ground that learned counsel for
the respondent no.3 did not consent for
it. The order was passed on 21.07.2020.
The recall application has been filed on
17.07.2023. There is only presumption
with regard to the judicial proceedings. It
is not any finding of fact. It is no opinion.

The order dated 21.07.2020 records
that "learned counsel for the petitioner
submitted that parties have amicably
settled the dispute and which learned
counsel for the respondent no.3 did not
contradict. In fact, what has been stated
on behalf of respondent no.3 has been
quoted in the Court's order. At the cost of
repetition the Court reproduces it once
again. The order speaks that "Learned
counsel for respondent no.3 does not
contradict the said fact and states that
in view of compromise between the
parties, respondent no.3 does not want
to pursue the present criminal
proceedings against the petitioner."
There is no reason to recall the
order dated 21.07.2020. The recall
application is dismissed.
Delay condonation application IA
No. 13694 of 2023 also stands dismissed
accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 27.09.2023
 Jitendra
